production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): its Temerario page shows only "2026 Lamborghini Temerario", and its 2025 address also shows the 2026 car (kbb-temerario-2025). Edmunds' first drive (edmunds-temerario-2026, Jonathan Elfalan, 25 July 2025) is of the "2026 Lamborghini Temerario". PistonHeads (pistonheads-temerario, 18 August 2024): "first deliveries expected in 2025". Still on sale.

configuration.note: Evo panel: "Engine | V8, 3995cc, twin-turbo, plus three 110kW e-motors"

aspiration.note: PistonHeads: "all-new 3,995cc, twin-turbo, dry-sumped 'hot-V' V8 called L411"

fuel.note: PistonHeads: "plug-in hybrid, four-wheel drive"; "3.8kWh battery pack" with "up to 7kW of charging rate possible". Lamborghini's US page lists an EPA "24 MPGe" electricity+gasoline rating.

drivetrain.note: PistonHeads: "plug-in hybrid, four-wheel drive" with an "e-4WD system including real torque vectoring" (electric front axle).

transmission.note: Evo: "an eight-speed DCT gearbox shared with the Revuelto"; PistonHeads: "The eight-speed DCT for Temerario is new".

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote (Lamborghini model page): "MAX POWER (COMBINED ICE+EE): 920 CV / 677kW". 920 CV x 0.98632 = 907 hp. Evo panel (evo-temerario): "Power | 907bhp (combined)"; KBB: "Horsepower-Combined | 907 @ 9000 RPM"; Edmunds: "a combined 907 hp". No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (guide step 4). Quote (Evo spec panel, review by Richard Meaden and John Barker): "Weight | 1690kg (dry) (545bhp/ton)". 1,690 x 2.20462 = 3,726 lb. PistonHeads (pistonheads-temerario): "Dry weight is claimed to be 1,690kg". No curb weight for the standard car (steps 1 and 2) and no optioned-car curb weight (step 3) was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine; Lamborghini's model page gives no weight. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options (Edmunds describes an optional Alleggerita package).
